1.4.41-158.comment: Sign 1 means 'Yield', so you must give way to other road users. Sign 2 gives you right of way at the next intersection. Sign 3 only warns of a danger.

1.4.41-159.question_text: What do you need to pay attention to with this traffic sign?

options.text: I must signal left
I can only continue left
I must not signal

1.4.41-159.comment: This traffic sign indicates the direction of travel. You can only turn left here. You must signal your change of direction.

1.4.41-160.question_text: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.text: I must drive past obstacles on the left
I'm required to turn left
I can't turn right before the sign

1.4.41-160.comment: This sign indicates which side you need to pass the obstacle on. You might see this sign at medians, bus stops, or construction sites. If you encounter it at an intersection, you can turn in the indicated direction.

1.4.41-161.question_text: What applies in the area 15 meters before and after this traffic sign?

options.text: - stop
- not obstruct boarding or alighting passengers
- park

1.4.41-161.comment: This sign indicates there's a stop for trams or buses. Drivers can't park their vehicles 15 meters before and after the sign. However, stopping for up to three minutes is allowed as long as it doesn't obstruct public transport or endanger passengers.

1.4.41-162.question_text: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.text: I must signal right
I may only continue right
I can also continue left

1.4.41-162.comment: The indicated driving direction is mandatory. Drivers must turn right before the sign and signal this to other road users by using their turn signal.

1.4.41-163.question_text: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.text: I must expect arriving and departing taxis
I may stop
I may park

1.4.41-163.comment: This sign indicates a taxi stand. Generally, stopping is prohibited for all other vehicles. Drivers must always expect arriving and departing taxis and passengers in this area.

1.4.41-164.question_text: What does this combination of traffic signs indicate?

options.text: - used by winter sports enthusiasts
- not to be driven on in winter
- to be used only with snow chains

1.4.41-164.comment: This is a warning sign indicating a 'hazard area' along with an additional sign saying 'winter sports allowed'. It shows that winter sports enthusiasts can use the road, and other road users should pay special attention.

1.4.41-165.question_text: What must you consider in this traffic situation?

options.text: - not cross
- cross to overtake
- cross if oncoming traffic allows

1.4.41-165.comment: You must not cross the lane marking (solid line) in the middle of the road. It's also not allowed to drive on it.

1.4.41-166.question_text: What should you keep in mind on this right of way road?

options.text: Parking is prohibited
The lane marking must not be crossed
Parking is allowed if there's at least 3 meters between a parked vehicle and the lane marking

1.4.41-166.comment: The solid line in the middle between both lanes prohibits crossing or driving over it. Additionally, parking on right of way roads is prohibited outside of built-up areas.

1.4.41-167.question_text: You want to overtake. What's correct?

options.text: - overtake
- not overtake
- only overtake if I stay in the right lane

1.4.41-167.comment: You may overtake as long as you don't endanger other road users. The one-sided lane marking allows you to cross the two lines from the side where the broken line is drawn.

1.4.41-168.question_text: As a resident, you want to enter a designated bike street. What must you consider?

options.text: Vehicles must not exceed 30 km/h
Bicycles may ride side by side
Bicycle traffic must not be obstructed

1.4.41-168.comment: The speed limit for traffic is 30 km/h. Bicycle traffic must not be endangered or obstructed. If necessary, motor vehicle traffic must further reduce speed. Riding side by side with bicycles is allowed.

1.4.41-169.question_text: Who is allowed to enter a designated street?

options.text: All cyclists
All visitors of residents
All moped riders

1.4.41-169.comment: Other vehicles besides bicycles are not allowed to use bike streets unless additional signs permit it. The additional sign allows residents to enter the bike street.

1.4.41-170.question_text: Your lane is marked with this traffic sign. What do you need to keep in mind?

options.text: I must drive at least 60 km/h if road and traffic conditions allow
I can use this lane only if my vehicle can and is allowed to drive at least 60 km/h
I must not drive faster than 60 km/h

1.4.41-170.comment: This traffic sign indicates the minimum speed. So, you need to drive at least 60 km/h if road and traffic conditions allow.

1.4.41-171.question_text: What is the maximum speed for vehicles in a zone marked like this?
1.4.41-171.comment: Cyclists, e-scooters, and other allowed vehicles can go a maximum of 30 km/h in bike zones.

1.4.42-001.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: - only at the next intersection or junction
- at all intersections and junctions of this road
- until the end of the town

1.4.42-001.comment: This traffic sign gives you right of way at a specific spot. So, the right of way for drivers is limited and doesn't apply generally.

1.4.42-005.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: Start of a highway
End of the highway
Start of a main road

1.4.42-005.comment: This sign indicates that the highway begins here. All the rules for this type of road come into effect.

1.4.42-101.question_text: Which traffic sign gives right of way at the next intersection?

options.text: Traffic sign 1
Traffic sign 2
Traffic sign 3

1.4.42-101.comment: Only traffic sign number 1 gives you right of way at the next intersection. Traffic sign number 2 indicates the end of the right of way road, and traffic sign number 3 regulates right of way at a narrow point.

1.4.42-102.question_text: Which traffic sign gives right of way?

options.text: Traffic sign 2
Traffic sign 1
Traffic sign 3

1.4.42-102.comment: The correct sign for right of way is number 2. Number 1 indicates a dangerous curve ahead, while number 3 indicates the number of a federal road.

1.4.42-104.question_text: What is allowed on right of way roads outside built-up areas?

options.text: Stopping at the right edge of the road
Parking on the shoulder
Parking on the road

1.4.42-104.comment: Outside built-up areas, you can: 1. stop at the right edge of the road; 2. park on a sufficiently paved shoulder. Parking on the road is not allowed as it can obstruct or endanger traffic, since vehicles move faster here than in built-up areas. A sufficiently paved shoulder is not considered part of the road, so you can use it for parking. If there's a chance to pull over onto a paved shoulder, you should use it for short stops.

options.text: A right of way road
A zone stopping ban
Previous route bans

1.4.42-106.comment: This traffic sign indicates a change in right of way rules. It marks the end of the previous right of way stretch. Similar signs include 'Yield!' and 'Stop! Yield!', which you can find at intersections.

1.4.42-107.question_text: How should you behave with this traffic sign?

options.text: You can only use your right of way if the narrow point is clear
Despite having right of way, you must be prepared to stop
You must give way to oncoming traffic

1.4.42-107.comment: This sign gives you right of way over oncoming traffic. The oncoming traffic must wait before the obstacle. However, you should be ready to stop if oncoming traffic is already in the narrow point. You must let them pass. You can continue with right of way if the narrow point is clear.

1.4.42-109.question_text: What is allowed with these traffic signs?

options.text: Residents with the corresponding numbered parking permit can park here
All residents can use any of these parking spaces
As long as there are other parking spaces available, anyone can use this parking space

1.4.42-109.comment: This traffic sign indicates a parking space that can only be used by residents with the corresponding numbered parking permit. Other road users cannot park there and must look for other parking options.

options.text: Yes, as a disabled person with an official parking permit
Yes, as a companion of blind people with an official parking permit
Yes, for short-term shopping

1.4.42-110.comment: There are special parking spaces for people with severe walking disabilities or for blind individuals. An official parking permit identifies the vehicles of these individuals or their companions. Even short parking in these areas is not allowed for other drivers.

1.4.42-111.question_text: What should you keep in mind when parking here?

options.text: You must not exceed the parking time on the ticket
The parking ticket must be clearly visible for checks
The parking ticket and parking disc are treated the same

1.4.42-111.comment: You can only park here with a valid parking ticket. Make sure to display the ticket clearly behind your front or rear windshield. Don't exceed the parking time indicated on the ticket. The parking disc does not replace the parking ticket; it's only valid when the parking meter is out of order.

1.4.42-112.question_text: Which vehicles are allowed to park here?

options.text: Vehicles up to 2.8 tons total weight
Motorcycles
Vehicles over 3.5 tons total weight

1.4.42-112.comment: The traffic sign regulates the parking situation for drivers. It allows parking partially on the sidewalk, shoulder, and green strip for vehicles weighing up to 2.8 tons.

1.4.42-116.question_text: What must be the minimum speed of a vehicle to use this road?

options.text: 61 km/h
51 km/h
81 km/h

1.4.42-116.comment: You need to be able to reach a minimum speed of 60 km/h with your vehicle on a highway. The start of a highway is always marked by a traffic sign.

1.4.42-119.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: A dead end
A underpass
A road closed to vehicle traffic

1.4.42-119.comment: This is a dead end. You can drive in normally, but the road ends, and you may need to maneuver a lot to turn around and exit.

1.4.42-120.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: A first aid station
A junction
A hazard area

1.4.42-120.comment: This traffic sign shows that there is a first aid station, like the 'Red Cross' or 'Samaritans', at this location. It does not indicate a hazard area.

1.4.42-125.question_text: What should you consider with this traffic sign?

options.text: The street lighting doesn't stay on all night
Vehicles can be parked here without lights all night
Vehicles are not allowed to park here

1.4.42-125.comment: If you see this sign on street lamps, you need to secure your vehicle with a parking light. Since these lamps don't stay on all night, an unlit car here is very unsafe in the dark.

1.4.42-126.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: A federal road
You must not drive faster than 35 km/h
You must drive at least 35 km/h

1.4.42-126.comment: This traffic sign indicates a federal road. The number shown refers to the specific federal road and not to a speed limit.

1.4.42-128.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: A usually less busy highway section
A point where you must leave the highway
A mandatory detour for vehicles carrying dangerous goods

1.4.42-128.comment: The diversion arrow indicates that you are on a highway section prone to traffic jams and shows an alternative route. However, you're not required to follow it.

1.4.42-129.question_text: You're driving with daytime running lights into a lit tunnel. What should you do?

options.text: I turn on the low beam
I don't need to turn on any lights
I turn on the parking lights

1.4.42-129.comment: As the driver, you need to turn on your low beam. Daytime running lights aren't enough because the light conditions in the tunnel aren't as bright as daylight. You're required to make your vehicle clearly visible.

1.4.42-131.question_text: What should you do with this traffic sign?

options.text: Take off your sunglasses
Turn on low beam
Turn on hazard lights

1.4.42-131.comment: This traffic sign is before the entrance to a tunnel. You should turn on your low beam and take off your sunglasses to ensure clear visibility.

1.4.42-132.question_text: You're driving into a well-lit tunnel marked like this. How should you behave?

options.text: I drive with low beam
I drive without lights
I drive with daytime running lights

1.4.42-132.comment: Even a well-lit tunnel doesn't have daylight conditions, so you need to enter with low beam to make your vehicle visible. Daytime running lights aren't enough here.

1.4.42-133.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: End of a traffic-calmed area
End of a pedestrian zone
End of a playground

1.4.42-133.comment: This sign indicates the end of a traffic-calmed area. Higher speed limits apply again. As a driver, you don't have right of way when leaving and need to be careful when entering.

1.4.42-134.question_text: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.text: Priority road
No parking outside built-up areas on the road
Motorway

1.4.42-134.comment: You're on a priority road. This sign is repeated at every intersection or junction where you have right of way. Outside built-up areas, parking on priority roads is not allowed. These roads are usually fast, and parked vehicles could cause hazards.

1.4.42-135.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: A numbered detour
Subway line 3
A numbered underground garage

1.4.42-135.comment: This sign shows a numbered detour. Since there are several detours, they are numbered so you know exactly where to go.

1.4.42-136.question_text: What should you pay attention to with this combination of traffic signs?

options.text: If I follow the priority road, I must signal left
If I go straight, I must signal right
Going left is mandatory

1.4.42-136.comment: The priority road is guided around the corner by the additional sign. It's a bending priority road. If you stay on the priority road, you need to signal. You must also watch for pedestrians crossing the road and stop if necessary. The answer 'Going left is mandatory' is incorrect because this sign doesn't dictate a direction.

1.4.42-138.question_text: How should you behave with this traffic sign?

options.text: I must approach at moderate speed if pedestrians want to cross
I must allow pedestrians to cross
I must not stop on the pedestrian crossing if traffic is heavy

1.4.42-138.comment: At pedestrian crossings, pedestrians have the right of way, so vehicles should always approach at moderate speed and be ready to brake. There's a strict no-overtaking rule at pedestrian crossings, and when traffic is heavy, you must not stop on the crossing.

options.text: That the flowing traffic will stop
That children will run across the road more often than usual
That children will play on the road under supervision

1.4.42-139.comment: The traffic sign 'Traffic helper', formerly known as school crossing guards, means that traffic helpers regulate traffic. They can stop traffic to allow children to cross the street. You should expect that flowing traffic will stop and children will run across the road more often.

1.4.42-140.question_text: What applies after this traffic sign?

options.text: I must drive at walking speed
I must not hinder pedestrians
I may only park in marked areas

1.4.42-140.comment: Within the traffic-calmed area, you can only drive at a maximum walking speed of 4 to 7 km/h, meaning first gear without pressing the gas. The street can be fully used by pedestrians. Children are allowed to play on the street. Be especially attentive and ready to brake. Pedestrians must not be hindered or endangered, and you may need to wait. Since playing on the street is allowed, you need to pay extra attention to children. You can only park in marked areas.

1.4.42-141.question_text: What does this combination of traffic signs mean for you?

options.text: I'm on a priority road that bends left
I must not turn right or go straight
I must observe the right of way of vehicles coming from the right if I go straight

1.4.42-141.comment: The traffic sign indicates the course of the priority road. The additional sign shows the bend to the left; if you follow this direction, you're still on the priority road.

1.4.42-142.question_text: What do you need to consider with this traffic sign?

options.text: Children can play on the entire street
Motor vehicles must drive at walking speed
Pedestrians can use the whole street width

1.4.42-142.comment: All three answers are correct. In a "calmed traffic area", pedestrians can use the whole street, children can play on the street, and you must only drive at walking speed.

1.4.42-143.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: A customs checkpoint
A toll road
A no-entry zone

1.4.42-143.comment: When you see this sign, you're approaching a customs checkpoint. This means you might hit a traffic jam, so you should slow down. You might also be checked, so it's best to have all your documents ready. Follow the customs officers' instructions.

options.text: - ends a built-up area
- begins a built-up area
- ends a detour

1.4.42-144.comment: The location sign shows on its back at the bottom that it marks the end of a built-up area. The top part points to the next built-up area. It's located on the left side of the road.

1.4.42-145.question_text: What do you need to consider in traffic situations like this?

options.text: - cross it to get around obstacles
- cross it to overtake
- not cross it if it endangers traffic

1.4.42-145.comment: Guidelines are meant to separate lanes. So, you can only cross them if you're going around obstacles or overtaking. This is only allowed if it doesn't endanger any other road users.

1.4.42-146.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: A rest area and breakdown bay
A temporary additional lane
A stopping area for breaks and driver changes

1.4.42-146.comment: If you're driving a vehicle, you can only stop in a rest area or breakdown bay in case of an emergency or breakdown.

1.4.42-147-M.question_text: You're driving on this road with a bike lane. How can you use the bike lane?

options.text: - use the bike lane if needed
- park on the bike lane
- stop on the bike lane

1.4.42-147-M.comment: You can use the bike lane if needed, as long as you don't endanger or obstruct cyclists.

1.4.43-101.question_text: What can red-and-white warning signs on vehicles indicate?

options.text: A trailer parked on the road in a built-up area
A vehicle with a wide load
A hazardous materials vehicle

1.4.43-101.comment: Red-and-white warning signs indicate vehicles with a wide load (like oversized agricultural vehicles). Trailers parked in built-up areas must be either lit or marked with reflective warning signs. So, these signs don't indicate a hazardous materials vehicle.

1.5.01-004.question_text: How does a significant drop in recommended tire pressure affect you?

options.text: Fuel consumption increases
Tire wear increases
Pollutant emissions decrease

1.5.01-004.comment: Low tire pressure leads to a significant increase in fuel consumption. The effort needed to keep the tire rolling is much higher than with the correct pressure. This causes more tire wear, higher fuel consumption, and harms the environment.

1.5.01-005.question_text: When should you turn off the engine to save fuel and reduce environmental impact?

options.text: When you have to wait in a traffic jam for a long time
When you have to wait at railway crossings or construction sites
When you stop at a 'STOP' sign

1.5.01-005.comment: To avoid unnecessary fuel consumption, you should turn off the engine in certain situations, like in traffic jams or at railway crossings. While starting the engine uses more fuel, this is balanced out after about a minute of idling. However, you shouldn't turn off the engine at a stop sign.

1.5.01-006.question_text: Your vehicle is leaking some oil. How much drinking water can become undrinkable from just one drop of oil?

options.text: 600 liters
50 liters
1 liter

1.5.01-006.comment: You should avoid oil leaks in your vehicle at all costs. Just one drop of oil can contaminate up to 600 liters of water and make it undrinkable.

1.5.01-007.question_text: What should you pay attention to when refueling?

options.text: Don't inhale fuel vapors
Don't top off if the tank is full and the pump has shut off
Fill the tank as full as possible

1.5.01-007.comment: Inhaling fuel vapors is harmful to your health. So, make sure to use the pump correctly and watch for any issues while refueling. When the tank is full, the automatic shut-off should engage to prevent overflow. Also, it's important to leave some air in the tank so the fuel can expand.

1.5.01-010.question_text: Where can you properly dispose of used oils, lubricants, and vehicle batteries?

options.text: At recycling centers
At car repair shops
In household trash

1.5.01-010.comment: Used oils, lubricants, and vehicle batteries can be disposed of properly at recycling centers or through car repair shops. You should never throw these materials in the household trash, as they are considered hazardous waste.

1.5.01-014.question_text: What measures help protect the environment?

options.text: - Low-resistance tires
- Low-friction oils
- Air conditioning systems

1.5.01-014.comment: Turning off the air conditioning saves fuel. Low-resistance tires are designed to reduce rolling resistance and can help save fuel. Low-friction oils are synthetic oils with improved flow characteristics, which help the engine lubricate better and reduce friction. This also leads to noticeable fuel savings. Always use oils approved by the engine or vehicle manufacturer to avoid engine damage.

1.5.01-016.question_text: What can regular vehicle maintenance contribute to?

options.text: Keeping fuel consumption low
Keeping emissions low
Ensuring traffic safety

1.5.01-016.comment: Regular vehicle maintenance helps ensure traffic safety, keeps fuel consumption low, and maintains low emissions.

1.5.01-110.question_text: How can you drive in an environmentally friendly way?

options.text: Ease off the gas in time and use momentum when the next traffic light is red
Avoid unnecessary acceleration and braking
Always accelerate fully at green

1.5.01-110.comment: Try to avoid constant acceleration and braking. Accelerating uses up a lot of fuel, which you can avoid when approaching red lights by easing off the gas. Full acceleration leads to higher emissions and noise pollution, which harms the environment.

1.5.01-114.question_text: What can help save fuel and reduce environmental impact?

options.text: Pay attention to fuel consumption when buying a vehicle
Drive predictably to contribute to smooth traffic flow
Use public transport, ride a bike, or walk whenever possible

1.5.01-114.comment: As a driver, you can check which car models use less fuel before making a purchase. Additionally, a fuel-efficient driving style also contributes to savings.

1.5.01-115.question_text: What can you do to protect the environment?

options.text: - Short trips
- Driving at full throttle
- Driving into crowded city centers

1.5.01-115.comment: The best way to protect the environment is to drive less. Avoid any trips that aren't necessary. Certain driving habits waste a lot of fuel: short trips, especially when the engine is still cold, stop-and-go traffic in crowded city centers, and searching for parking. Additionally, in high-traffic areas, the risk of smog increases with every vehicle that emits pollutants. Driving at full throttle not only creates noise but also significantly increases your fuel consumption. However, if you stay just 20% below the maximum speed, you can reduce your fuel consumption by about 40%. Carpooling is also a great way to help the environment.

1.5.01-118.question_text: Why is using low-friction oils beneficial?

options.text: - Creates less friction in the engine
- Reduces fuel consumption
- Can be disposed of in household trash

1.5.01-118.comment: Low-friction oils have better flow characteristics. They are synthetic oils that reduce friction in the engine and optimize lubrication due to their improved viscosity. This helps save fuel. When using low-friction oils, make sure they are approved by the engine or vehicle manufacturer.

options.text: - Remove unnecessary roof racks
- Drive predictably
- Use winter tires year-round

1.5.01-120.comment: You can save fuel by: 1. driving smoothly and predictably while avoiding high RPMs; 2. removing unused roof racks, as they increase air resistance and fuel consumption; 3. switching from winter to summer tires in warm weather. Smooth driving means avoiding unnecessary acceleration and braking. For example, rolling slowly toward a red light lets you use momentum if it turns green before you reach it. Just having to accelerate saves fuel compared to starting from a complete stop.

1.5.01-121.question_text: How can you reduce tire wear?

options.text: I try to avoid hard acceleration
I regularly check tire pressure
I use winter tires year-round

1.5.01-121.comment: Driving with winter tires in non-winter conditions leads to increased tire wear. Hard acceleration is also associated with higher wear. Always maintain the recommended tire pressure from the vehicle manufacturer. Low tire pressure significantly increases tire wear. With insufficient air pressure, the tire deforms more with each rotation than it would at the correct pressure, causing the tire's fabric layers to rub against each other. This can generate heat that irreparably damages the tire.

1.5.01-122.question_text: Which vehicles are generally exempt from the traffic ban for 'environmental zones'?

options.text: Agricultural and forestry tractors
Ambulances on duty
All vehicles of residents in environmental zones

1.5.01-122.comment: The traffic ban for 'environmental zones' generally doesn't apply to ambulances that are on duty. Agricultural and forestry tractors are also not affected.

1.5.01-123.question_text: When is it sensible to turn off a combustion engine?

options.text: When waiting a long time at railway crossings
When loading and unloading the vehicle
When stopping at intersections with a stop sign

1.5.01-123.comment: Longer wait times at a closed railway crossing and when loading or unloading justify turning off a combustion engine. This saves fuel and reduces noise. The wait at a stop sign is usually short, and you can drive on soon after letting cross traffic go, so you typically don't turn off the engine then.

1.5.01-124.question_text: You're driving in city traffic during rush hour. What effect does stop-and-go driving have?

options.text: - uses more fuel
- produces more emissions
- causes more disturbances for others

1.5.01-124.comment: Fuel consumption is higher in stop-and-go traffic because you have to brake and accelerate more often. This leads to more emissions and can disturb other road users.

1.5.01-125.question_text: What is a requirement for environmentally friendly and fuel-efficient driving?

options.text: Regularly checking tire pressure
Regular vehicle maintenance
Regular engine washing

1.5.01-125.comment: Tire pressure has a big impact on fuel consumption since it affects rolling resistance. Regular vehicle maintenance helps keep fuel consumption low and emissions down.

1.5.01-126.question_text: You're driving a vehicle with a manual transmission. Which driving style leads to high fuel consumption in the city?

options.text: Rapid acceleration
Driving at high engine speeds
Driving in a high gear

1.5.01-126.comment: Rapid acceleration uses more fuel than normal acceleration. The higher the engine speed, the more fuel is consumed.

1.5.01-127.question_text: You're driving a vehicle with a manual transmission. How can you reduce your vehicle's fuel consumption?

options.text: By shifting to higher gears early
By driving predictively to avoid frequent speed changes
By driving at high engine speeds

1.5.01-127.comment: The higher the engine speed, the more fuel is consumed. By driving predictively, you can avoid unnecessary acceleration and braking.

1.5.01-128.question_text: How can you reduce the noise caused by your vehicle?

options.text: By driving at low engine speeds
By using low-noise tires
By removing the air filter element

1.5.01-128.comment: The higher the engine speed, the louder the engine gets. Tires can vary in quality, so pay attention to the noise level when buying tires.

1.5.01-129.question_text: What should you do to protect the environment?

options.text: - have your vehicle checked if there's excessive smoke from the exhaust
- turn off the engine when waiting for a long time
- avoid unnecessary back-and-forth driving

1.5.01-129.comment: Even when standing still, the engine burns fuel, so you should turn it off during longer stops. If you notice unusual signs like smoke, you should have your vehicle checked.

1.5.01-130.question_text: You're driving a vehicle with a manual transmission. What can cause avoidable noise pollution while driving?

options.text: By accelerating unnecessarily hard
By having a faulty muffler
By driving fast in low gears

1.5.01-130.comment: The higher the engine speed, the louder the engine gets. Tuned exhaust systems are usually louder than standard ones. Rapid acceleration also uses more fuel than normal acceleration.

1.5.01-131.question_text: You're driving a vehicle with a manual transmission on a flat road. How should you shift to drive in an environmentally friendly and fuel-efficient way?

options.text: Shift up as early as possible
Shift down as late as possible
Run the gears up to the high RPM range and then shift

1.5.01-131.comment: Try to keep the engine speed as low as possible while accelerating. When coasting, shift down as late as possible to make use of engine braking and minimize brake use.

1.5.01-132.question_text: You're driving a vehicle with a manual transmission. Which behavior harms the environment?

options.text: An uneven driving style
Frequent revving while waiting at a red light
Driving downhill in a high gear

1.5.01-132.comment: Maintaining a constant speed uses less fuel than constantly speeding up and slowing down. Revving the engine at a red light wastes fuel.

1.5.01-133.question_text: You're driving a vehicle with a manual transmission. How can you achieve fuel efficiency?

options.text: By having the right tire pressure
By driving smoothly at low engine RPM
By shifting up late while accelerating

1.5.01-133.comment: Driving at a constant speed uses less fuel than constantly speeding up and slowing down. Tire pressure greatly affects fuel consumption because it influences rolling resistance.

1.5.01-134.question_text: What should you pay attention to after starting your vehicle?

options.text: - drive off immediately
- drive at low engine RPM
- let the engine warm up while idling

1.5.01-134.comment: Idling with the engine running unnecessarily harms the environment. Start the engine only if you're ready to drive. The lower the engine RPM, the less fuel is burned.

1.7.01-003.question_text: What affects the size of the centrifugal force in curves?

options.text: The curve radius
The speed
The wind

1.7.01-003.comment: Centrifugal force can throw your vehicle out of a curve. Doubling your speed quadruples the centrifugal force. The tighter the curve, the greater the centrifugal force, so you need to brake early in sharp curves.

1.8.01-003.question_text: When are violations recorded in the driving suitability register that are rated with two points removed?

options.text: - after 5 years
- after 3 years
- after 2 years

1.8.01-003.comment: Violations recorded in the driving suitability register with two points are removed after five years. Serious offenses are always penalized with two points.

2.1.01-001.question_text: What can cause skidding in curves?

options.text: Defective shock absorbers
Too low or uneven tire pressure
Insufficient loading

2.1.01-001.comment: Defective shock absorbers can cause a vehicle to skid or lose control in curves. Correct tire pressure is crucial for stability in curves. Too low or uneven tire pressure reduces stability and increases the risk of skidding. Overloading affects stability, but underloading isn't a concern.

options.text: Cutting corners
Late dimming of headlights
Too much distance in front

2.1.01-004.comment: Cutting corners means steering your vehicle inward in a curve and using the opposite lane to go faster, which poses a serious risk to oncoming traffic and can lead to severe accidents. Late dimming can also endanger oncoming drivers by blinding them.

options.text: I reduce my speed so the overtaking vehicle can merge in front of me
I speed up so the overtaking vehicle can merge behind me
I maintain my speed since the safety distance is sufficient

2.1.01-007-M.comment: The overtaking driver likely can't complete their maneuver as planned. To prevent an accident, you should let them merge.

2.1.01-102.question_text: What does listening to loud music, especially with heavy bass, in the car lead to?

options.text: Nearby blind people lose their orientation
The driver's attention is significantly impaired
Blind people can more easily recognize the road's course

2.1.01-102.comment: Loud music in the car has two negative effects: it distracts the driver and makes it hard to focus on traffic. Deep bass can confuse blind pedestrians, making it difficult for them to orient themselves.

2.1.01-103.question_text: What can create a hazard while driving?

options.text: A heavily biased braking system
Too much play in the steering
A non-functioning low beam

2.1.01-103.comment: If the low beam isn't working, you won't see well and others won't see you. A biased braking system can cause the vehicle to skid or have a longer braking distance. Too much play in the steering means your steering commands won't be executed properly.

2.1.02-002.question_text: You're driving on a narrow road. About 20 meters ahead, a child suddenly runs onto the road. When is a collision unavoidable even with emergency braking?

options.text: 50 km/h
30 km/h
20 km/h

2.1.02-002.comment: To answer this question, you first need to calculate the reaction distance and the emergency braking distance. At 50 km/h, the reaction distance is 50 / 10 x 3 = 15 meters. So, the reaction distance is 15 meters. The emergency braking distance is calculated as follows: (50 / 10 x 50 / 10) / 2 = 12.5. So, 50 km/h is the correct answer.

2.1.02-003.question_text: Why do you need to brake?

options.text: Because a person is running onto the road
Because passengers are getting off the tram
Because the truck is changing into my lane

2.1.02-003.comment: In the video, you can see a person (coming from the right) running onto the road. Pay attention to this and brake in time.

options.text: I stop
I continue driving as before
I accelerate

2.1.02-004.comment: When turning right, you always need to watch out for pedestrians or cyclists. They are allowed to cross the road in front of you.

2.1.02-005-M.question_text: What should you expect in this situation?

options.text: Children running onto the road
People getting off on the roadside
There’s a pedestrian crossing ahead

2.1.02-005-M.comment: The traffic sign indicates that you should be extra cautious of children who might run onto the road between vehicles. You also need to expect that people might get off on the roadside.

2.1.03-015.question_text: What can lead to aquaplaning (water slick) on a wet road?

options.text: High speed
Worn tires
Ruts in the road

2.1.03-015.comment: Aquaplaning, also known as water slick, happens when the tread depth of the tires is too low to displace the accumulated water, or when the amount of water to be displaced is too large due to high speed (from 60 km/h). Additionally, ruts in the road where water collects can further contribute to this effect.

2.1.03-017-B.question_text: Why can overtaking be dangerous here?

options.text: Because there's slush on the overtaking lane
Because thrown-up slush can obstruct visibility
Because the road under the slush may be icy

2.1.03-017-B.comment: Overtaking in slush carries many dangers. There could be an ice layer under the snow, making overtaking risky. Plus, you might throw slush onto other vehicles or lose control yourself.

2.1.03-018.question_text: How should you behave if your vehicle is hit by strong crosswinds?

options.text: Steer against it
Reduce speed
Accelerate sharply

2.1.03-018.comment: If your vehicle is hit by strong crosswinds, you should definitely not accelerate, but instead reduce your speed and steer against it. The faster you go, the harder it can be to keep your vehicle on the road, as crosswinds can cause it to skid.

options.text: Your vehicle can be pushed left by the strong crosswind
When you overtake, your vehicle will be pulled right when entering the truck's slipstream
The vehicle in front of you can be pushed right

2.1.03-021-B.comment: When driving on the highway in strong crosswinds from the right, the wind constantly pushes your car to the left. You need to steer right to stay in your lane. When you overtake a truck, expect that the wind pressure will suddenly disappear as you enter the truck's slipstream. If you keep steering against it, there's a risk of hitting the truck on the right. Since the crosswind comes from the right, the vehicle in front of you could be pushed to the left.

2.1.03-023.question_text: Why do you need to reduce speed in heavy rain?

options.text: Because the braking distance increases
Because visibility worsens
Because aquaplaning (water slick) can occur

2.1.03-023.comment: Water on the windshield or visor breaks the light and worsens visibility, and splashed-up water also obstructs your view. The braking distance is longer on wet roads due to less grip. The tread of the tires channels the water away. At high speeds, the amount of water to be displaced becomes too large, leading to the risk of aquaplaning, where there’s no contact between the road and the tires. You can't control the vehicle anymore.

2.1.03-025.question_text: What can a sudden deterioration of the road condition lead to?

options.text: To skidding and slipping hazards
To changed tire noises
To longer reaction times

2.1.03-025.comment: When the road surface deteriorates, it always results in a change and worsening of grip. As the tires lose traction, the vehicle can skid and slip more easily. Tire noises also depend on the condition of the road surface and change when the road, for example, goes from asphalt to cobblestones.

2.1.03-027.question_text: What special things should you consider when driving on tree-lined roads?

options.text: Curves are often particularly tight and unclear
Narrow road width and its often curved shape require extra caution with oncoming traffic
The trees provide side protection

2.1.03-027.comment: The road is usually very narrow and often curved to let rainwater drain off. So, you need to be especially careful with oncoming traffic. Curves can be hard to see because of the trees, so take extra care when entering curves, especially left turns. The trees don't provide any protection for drivers, not even from the wind.

options.text: I brake
I drive as far right as possible
I stay in the middle of my lane

2.1.03-028.comment: While overtaking a cyclist, an oncoming truck might partially enter your lane. So, slow down and drive as far right as you can.

options.text: - green car
- blue car
- tractor

2.1.03-029.comment: You can barely see a green car coming from the right. So, please brake in time because, in these road conditions, your braking distance can increase significantly.

2.1.03-030.question_text: Why do you need to be ready to stop here?

options.text: Because of the truck
Because of the motorcyclist

2.1.03-030.comment: Since the road is very narrow and your view is blocked by the tree (on the front left), you should be prepared to stop because of the truck.

2.1.03-033.question_text: How should you behave correctly now?

options.text: I reduce my speed
I avoid sudden steering movements
I steer sharply to the right

2.1.03-033.comment: Due to the bad weather conditions, you should reduce your speed and avoid sudden steering movements (as indicated by the warning sign), otherwise, you could skid.

options.text: Limited steering ability of the vehicle
Reduced braking ability of the vehicle
Increased tire grip

2.1.03-034.comment: During aquaplaning, your vehicle loses direct contact with the road surface, so you can't steer or brake effectively.

2.1.03-036.question_text: How should you behave correctly in this situation?

options.text: I reduce my speed
I avoid sudden steering
I brake hard

2.1.03-036.comment: The traffic sign indicates a risk of skidding and slipping. To avoid skidding, you should reduce your speed, especially when it's raining and leaves are falling on the road. Hard braking, rapid acceleration, or sudden steering can cause your tires to lose grip, leading to skidding.

2.1.03-037.question_text: What should you prepare for here?

options.text: A longer braking distance
Poor visibility of my vehicle
Increased tire grip

2.1.03-037.comment: Because of the rain, you should expect that other road users might not see your vehicle well, and your braking distance will increase due to reduced tire grip.

2.1.03-038.question_text: When are you particularly at risk during the overtaking maneuver here?

options.text: When entering the truck's slipstream
When exiting the truck's slipstream
When changing lanes after overtaking

2.1.03-038.comment: If there's strong crosswind from the right, you're particularly at risk when you move from open road into the slipstream of a truck during an overtaking maneuver. The strong wind pushes your vehicle to the left, causing you to steer against it. While overtaking, you enter the truck's slipstream, and the crosswind disappears, so you need to adjust your steering. Once you exit the slipstream, the crosswind pressure returns, and you have to steer against it again.

2.1.03-101.question_text: Where does aquaplaning occur most frequently?

options.text: In road depressions
At ruts in the road
At level crossings

2.1.03-101.comment: Aquaplaning happens when your speed is too high and/or there's more water than your tire treads can handle. A layer of water prevents tire contact with the road, making the vehicle uncontrollable. The risk of aquaplaning is particularly high in ruts and road depressions. At level crossings, there's usually no increased risk of aquaplaning since water can drain well there.

2.1.03-103.question_text: What should you expect when it starts to rain after a long dry spell?

options.text: A dangerous slippery layer on the road
Worse visibility right after turning on the wipers
A shorter braking distance

2.1.03-103.comment: When it starts to rain after a long dry period, a slippery film forms on the road that only washes away after a while. This film is more dangerous than rain alone. Brake very carefully. This slippery film also builds up on your windshield, making visibility worse right after you turn on the wipers. The braking distance increases because of the reduced grip.

2.1.03-104.question_text: It starts to rain. Why do you need to increase your following distance immediately?

options.text: Because a slippery film can form, increasing the braking distance
Because visibility can get worse and the wipers won't clear the view right away
Because the brakes respond faster

2.1.03-104.comment: When it starts to rain, you need to increase your following distance for several reasons: Wet conditions turn dirt, dust, and fine debris on the road into a dangerous slippery film. This reduces grip and increases braking distance. This slippery film also forms on your windshield and brake drums. When you activate the wipers, they can smear the glass and impair your visibility. On brake drums, this film can slow down brake response in wet conditions.

2.1.03-105.question_text: You're driving on a federal road outside of town in thick fog. Are you allowed to drive over the center line constantly?

options.text: No, because it can endanger oncoming traffic
Yes, if fog lights and rear fog lights are on
Yes, because it reduces the risk of going off the road

2.1.03-105.comment: Driving on the center line is not allowed even in thick fog, especially since drivers may collide with oncoming traffic due to reduced visibility. Slow down in fog and stay close to the right edge of the road for a safe drive.

2.1.03-106.question_text: What should you do during the day when a fog bank suddenly appears?

options.text: Immediately adjust your speed to the visibility conditions
Turn on your low beam headlights
Only turn on your parking lights

2.1.03-106.comment: As a driver, you must turn on your low beam headlights during the day in fog, snowfall, and other poor visibility conditions. Driving with just parking lights is not allowed because they don't provide enough light. Adjust your speed to the visibility and use your fog lights if visibility is under 50 meters.

2.1.03-107.question_text: How can you ensure good visibility through the windshield?

options.text: In fog, turn on the wipers from time to time
In slushy snow, turn on the wipers before other vehicles throw slush on your windshield
When the inside of the windshield fogs up, turn off the ventilation and keep the windows closed

2.1.03-107.comment: In fog, set your wipers to intermittent to remove fine water droplets. Before overtaking or being overtaken, adjust your wipers to clear any slush or spray immediately. To avoid fogging inside the windshield, set the ventilation to bring in outside air instead of recirculating. Crack the windows slightly to let moisture escape. Briefly turning on the air conditioning can quickly dehumidify the air.

2.1.03-110.question_text: What should you keep in mind in this situation?

options.text: Speed should be adjusted due to visibility conditions
Estimating distances is difficult due to the constant change of light and shadow
The constant change of light and shadow makes it hard to see other road users in time

2.1.03-110.comment: When there's a sudden and strong change in light conditions, you need to reduce your speed because your eyes can't adjust quickly enough. Other road users or obstacles can be very hard to see in the dark areas.

2.1.03-111.question_text: You've found yourself in this situation while overtaking several trucks. How do you behave now?

options.text: I cancel the overtaking maneuver
I ensure a safe following distance after merging back in
I continue to overtake quickly and merge in front of the red truck

2.1.03-111.comment: Visibility is very poor due to the weather, and the road isn't clearly visible. To avoid endangering anyone, you should cancel the overtaking maneuver as quickly as possible and ensure a safe distance when merging back in.

options.text: I continue to slow down
I wait before the obstacle
I switch to the left now

2.1.03-115.comment: Since a vehicle is coming from behind in the left lane, please wait before the obstacle (snow drift ahead) and continue to slow down.

options.text: - reduce speed significantly
- continue driving in my lane
- drive left past the road damage

2.1.03-116-M.comment: Here, you should significantly reduce your speed due to poor visibility and continue driving in your lane. Passing on the left is not a good idea, as someone might be coming from the opposite direction.

2.1.03-117.question_text: You're driving on the highway. What is correct in this situation?

options.text: - turn on the rear fog light
- drive no faster than 50 km/h
- drive no faster than 80 km/h

2.1.03-117.comment: With severely limited visibility on the highway, you can turn on your rear fog light and drive no faster than 50 km/h.

2.1.03-119.question_text: You're using your car's Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) during this weather. What should you expect?

options.text: The ACC might not work properly
I need to control the speed and distance myself
The ACC will stop the vehicle

2.1.03-119.comment: The Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) estimates the distance and speed of the car in front. In bad weather, like snow and dirt, its function can be limited. So, you need to manage the distance and speed yourself.

2.1.03-120.question_text: You're driving on a narrow avenue. What should you keep in mind?

options.text: I should be able to stop within half the visible distance
I might need to stop for oncoming traffic
I should expect uneven road edges from tree roots

2.1.03-120.comment: The narrow road and its often curved shape due to tree roots require extra caution in turns and with oncoming traffic. Choose your speed so you can stop within half the distance you can see. For example, if you can see about 40 meters ahead, you should be able to stop within about 20 meters. At 30 km/h, the stopping distance is around 18 meters.

2.1.03-121.question_text: The indicator for the Electronic Stability Control (ESC) has lit up several times. How should you react in this situation?

options.text: I reduce my speed, as it’s too high
I maintain my speed, as the ESC system allows for safe driving
I go to a workshop, as the ESC indicator suggests a defect

2.1.03-121.comment: You need to reduce your speed. The slippery road and your obviously too high speed for the current conditions can cause the wheels to lose grip, and your car could skid.

options.text: With pedestrians on the road
With reduced space from oncoming traffic
With glare from the low sun

2.1.03-122.comment: The snow on the sides of the road can narrow the driving lane. So, you should expect that the space between you and oncoming traffic is reduced. Also, the traffic sign indicates there's a parking area for hikers on the right, so you should expect pedestrians on the road.

2.1.03-123.question_text: While driving straight, you lose control of your vehicle due to aquaplaning. How should you react?

options.text: I gently lift my foot off the gas pedal
I keep the steering wheel as straight as possible
I brake hard

2.1.03-123.comment: During aquaplaning, you can't steer or change direction. You should neither accelerate nor brake. So, just gently lift your foot off the gas and try to keep the steering wheel straight until your tires regain contact with the road.

2.1.04-002.question_text: What should you do if wild animals suddenly appear in your high beams?

options.text: Switch to low beams immediately
Honk and brake
Keep driving with high beams unchanged

2.1.04-002.comment: Hold the steering wheel firmly and brake. Switch off the high beams, as they can blind the animals and cause them to stay on the road. Honk to scare them away. Avoid swerving at high speeds, as that can lead to hitting a tree or oncoming traffic. So, when you see wild animals on the road: brake, switch to low beams, and then honk to scare them away.

2.1.04-102.question_text: At night and in the rain, vehicles with low beams are coming towards you on a country road. What should you consider?

options.text: You might be blinded by reflections on the wet road
Visibility worsens due to streaks on the windshield
You can avoid glare by turning on high beams

2.1.04-102.comment: You shouldn't turn on your high beams in this situation, as that can blind oncoming traffic. Especially on wet roads, light reflections are significantly increased. Other issues include water droplets and streaks on the windshield that scatter the light and impair visibility.

2.1.04-103.question_text: What dangers can arise if you drive with your high beams on?

options.text: Oncoming drivers will be blinded
Wild animals on the road will be blinded and stay in the light
Abandoned vehicles on my side of the road will be recognized too late

2.1.04-103.comment: With your high beams on, you can blind drivers ahead and coming towards you, which might cause them to miss pedestrians and cyclists. Wild animals crossing the road can also be blinded, causing them to freeze in the light. You yourself will notice abandoned vehicles more easily with high beams.

2.1.04-104.question_text: At night on a country road, you see people on your side of the road. How should you behave if you're blinded by an oncoming vehicle?

options.text: - look towards the right edge of the road
- stop if necessary
- turn on high beams

2.1.04-104.comment: If you see people on the road at night, reduce your speed. Regularly looking at the road edge is ideal to avoid an accident. If you're also blinded, you can pull over to the right and stop.

2.1.05-001.question_text: You've been driving at high speed for a long time. What effects can this have?

options.text: The sense of speed decreases
Concentration ability decreases
The sense of the right speed for curves increases

2.1.05-001.comment: You quickly get used to high speeds and feel like you're in a rush in your car. This can be dangerous, especially at highway exits, as your concentration and reaction time can drop quickly. So, make sure to check your speed regularly!

2.1.05-002.question_text: What can long driving at higher speeds lead to?

options.text: You lose your sense of speed
You tailgate too closely
Your reaction readiness increases

2.1.05-002.comment: When you drive fast for a long time, your senses get used to it, and you start underestimating your speed. This is why people often take sharp turns off the highway too quickly. Fast, monotonous driving can reduce your concentration and reaction time. Often, drivers ignore the safe distance and tailgate.

2.1.05-005.question_text: What can lead to a dangerous underestimation of your own speed?

options.text: Long driving at higher speeds
Driving on a wide, well-built road
Loud engine and tire noise

2.1.05-005.comment: Wide and clear roads without changing surroundings can make you underestimate your speed. Long drives at higher speeds, like on the highway, can also cause this effect. Loud engine and tire noises can actually make you more aware of how fast you're going.

2.1.05-008.question_text: You're approaching a tight left turn at high speed. Why do you need to slow down before the turn?

options.text: You could slide out of the curve to the right
You could skid
You could slide out of the curve to the left

2.1.05-008.comment: At high speed, centrifugal force can cause your vehicle to slide out of the curve to the right and skid. That's why you should slow down before the turn.

2.1.05-009.question_text: In what situation is your own speed often underestimated?

options.text: On wide and well-built roads
After a long drive at higher speeds
On narrow roads with uneven surfaces

2.1.05-009.comment: When you drive steadily at high speeds, your concentration decreases. You get used to the speed. Wide roads with little surrounding development can also make you less aware of how fast you're actually going. Your reaction time gets longer.

2.1.05-101.question_text: What is particularly important when choosing your speed on narrow avenues?

options.text: Estimating the side distance to trees and oncoming traffic
That you might have to stop in the visible distance for oncoming wide vehicles
Quickly changing light conditions make estimating side distances easier

2.1.05-101.comment: When driving on narrow avenues, you need to consider factors like changing light conditions due to the trees. This makes it harder to judge the distances to the sides and oncoming traffic. You should choose a speed that allows you to stop within the distance you can see ahead. This is especially important since wide or tall vehicles often drive in the middle of the road.

2.1.05-103.question_text: Where should you expect sudden dangerous situations?

options.text: In forest areas
Behind hills
In front of schools

2.1.05-103.comment: You should expect sudden dangerous situations when: 1. visibility is severely limited; 2. people or animals might unexpectedly appear on the road. In low visibility, you might not see obstacles like stalled vehicles in time. You have less time to react. In forest areas, be cautious of wild animals during twilight; in residential areas, watch for children playing who might run onto the road. Be careful near schools and bus stops too.

2.1.05-104-M.question_text: Why do you need to reduce your speed here?

options.text: Because of the overtaking vehicle
Because of the speed limit
Because of the low traffic volume

2.1.05-104-M.comment: The vehicle dangerously overtaking in front of you poses a risk of collision. To avoid getting involved in an accident and to give other vehicles space to maneuver, you need to slow down.

2.1.05-105-M.question_text: What should you expect in this situation?

options.text: A slow-moving vehicle in my lane
Oncoming traffic cutting the corner
Wild animals crossing

2.1.05-105-M.comment: Since visibility is severely limited, be on the lookout for oncoming traffic cutting the corner, a slow-moving vehicle in your lane, and wild animals crossing.

2.1.06-002.question_text: Why can it be dangerous if you're the last in a line of vehicles and you immediately overtake after oncoming traffic has just cleared?

options.text: Because you have to expect others will also pull out to overtake
Because the overtaking distance might not be enough
Because needing to merge back into the line could cause an accident

2.1.06-002.comment: When a line of vehicles forms, you should generally overtake in order. The last vehicle in the line has the longest overtaking distance and must also expect that vehicles in front may pull out to overtake.

2.1.06-004-B.question_text: Are you allowed to overtake the black car on the right on this highway?

options.text: No, because there's no line of vehicles in the left lane
Yes, as long as you don't exceed 80 km/h
Yes, because there's enough space to overtake

2.1.06-004-B.comment: In this case, you cannot overtake the black car on the right. On highways and major roads, you can only overtake on the right in exceptional cases, like when there's a line of vehicles on the left.

2.1.06-005-B.question_text: The cars are going about 30 km/h. Can you overtake both before the curve?

options.text: Your overtaking distance would be too long
the bright car might pull out to overtake
the broken line can't be crossed

2.1.06-005-B.comment: You can cross the broken line. However, overtaking here would still be too dangerous because the distance before the curve is too short. You also need to consider that the driver of the bright car might try to overtake.

2.1.06-007-M.question_text: You want to overtake. What should you do now?

options.text: I give up on overtaking
I speed up
I maintain my speed

2.1.06-007-M.comment: Since the vehicle behind you has already started to overtake, you should give up on overtaking.

2.1.06-008-M.question_text: You want to overtake. What should you pay attention to?

options.text: only if I can see the required distance
only if no vehicle is coming towards me
at the same time as the blue car

2.1.06-008-M.comment: You can overtake if you can see the required distance and if no vehicle is coming towards you (limited visibility).

2.1.06-010.question_text: You're being overtaken and oncoming traffic is dangerously close. Still, the other vehicle continues to overtake. What do you do?

options.text: I reduce my speed
I maintain my speed
I increase my speed

2.1.06-010.comment: You need to slow down and move as far to the right as possible so the overtaking driver can safely pull back in. You should never increase your speed when being overtaken.

2.1.06-011.question_text: Why do you need to brake hard now?

options.text: Because of the car
Because of the truck
Because of the tractor

2.1.06-011.comment: Since the blue car is likely to come into your lane, you need to brake hard immediately and stay as far to the right as possible.

options.text: I overtake the blue car and then switch to the middle lane
I overtake the red van and then switch to the middle lane
I signal the following driver to keep more distance by lightly braking

2.1.06-012-M.comment: As the driver, you don't need to move to the middle lane just because another car is pressuring you from behind or using their high beams. You should overtake the blue car and the red van as usual. To safely switch to the middle lane, you need to complete the overtaking first.

2.1.06-013.question_text: You want to overtake. How should you behave correctly now?

options.text: I cancel the overtaking and stay behind the truck
I speed up and continue overtaking quickly
I maintain my speed and continue overtaking

2.1.06-013.comment: You've already signaled and want to overtake the truck. In your rearview mirror, you see a red car approaching quickly in the left lane. You need to immediately cancel the overtaking and stay behind the truck. If you continue, you could force the red car to brake hard, which might lead to a collision.

options.text: I continue the overtaking quickly
I cancel the overtaking and pull back to the right
I brake but continue the overtaking

2.1.06-014.comment: When vehicles are approaching quickly from behind, stay calm, finish the overtaking, and clear the lane at the next opportunity.

options.text: I overtake the van and then switch to the middle lane
I immediately switch to the right lane
I signal the following driver to keep more distance by lightly braking

2.1.06-015.comment: A driver in a car is tailgating you dangerously in the left lane and is signaling their intention to overtake with their high beams. You should overtake the van in the middle lane and then position yourself in front of it to ease the situation.

2.1.06-017-M.question_text: Why do you need to slow down here?

options.text: Because of the overtaking car
Because the speed limit is 80 km/h
Because of the tractor

2.1.06-017-M.comment: The oncoming car is overtaking despite the oncoming traffic about 250 meters ahead of you. You need to reduce your speed and move to the far right. This way, you ease the situation and give the overtaking car more time and space to finish overtaking and merge back in. The tractor is moving away from the intersection and poses no danger.

options.text: I slow down
I drive as far right as possible
I speed up

2.1.06-018-M.comment: If you're overtaking a vehicle while there's oncoming traffic, you should slow down and try to stay as far right as possible. This gives the other vehicle enough space to complete the overtaking safely.

2.1.06-021-M.question_text: You want to overtake. How should you behave correctly now?

options.text: I don't overtake the truck because I can't see the necessary distance
I follow the motorcycle since the truck is signaling an overtaking opportunity
I reduce the distance to the truck so I can overtake faster

2.1.06-021-M.comment: You shouldn't overtake the truck because you can't see the necessary distance.

2.1.06-022-M.question_text: Why do you have to stop the overtaking maneuver?

options.text: Because the tractor wants to turn left
Because oncoming traffic could be obstructed
Because a no-overtaking sign is in sight

2.1.06-022-M.comment: You should stop the overtaking maneuver because the tractor wants to turn left and oncoming traffic could be obstructed.

2.1.06-023-M.question_text: How should you behave correctly now?

options.text: - not, because the tractor will pull left
- carefully, since the tractor is signaling me to do so
- immediately, since the overtaking path is sufficient

2.1.06-023-M.comment: You shouldn't overtake because the tractor will pull left (see blinker).

2.1.06-024-M.question_text: You want to overtake. How should you behave correctly here?

options.text: I don't overtake because the yellow vehicle could be overtaking
I don't overtake because oncoming traffic could appear
I overtake because there's no oncoming traffic visible

2.1.06-024-M.comment: The right behavior (looking ahead) here is not to overtake because the yellow vehicle could be overtaking and oncoming traffic could appear (limited visibility).

2.1.06-025-M.question_text: How should you behave correctly now?

options.text: I brake immediately
I drive as far right as possible
I continue driving as usual

2.1.06-025-M.comment: Since a vehicle is on your lane, you should brake immediately and drive as far right as possible to avoid a collision.

2.1.06-026-M.question_text: Why are you not allowed to overtake now?

options.text: - motorcycle
- road layout
- red cars

2.1.06-026-M.comment: You can't overtake the cyclist because of the motorcycle (oncoming traffic) and the road layout, which results in poor visibility.

2.1.06-027-M.question_text: Why are you not allowed to overtake now?

options.text: - motorcycle
- red cars
- posted no-overtaking sign

2.1.06-027-M.comment: At this moment, a motorcyclist is passing the tractor. Wait until you can start the overtaking maneuver safely.

2.1.06-028-M.question_text: Why are you not allowed to overtake here?

options.text: - I can't see the further road layout well enough
- I can't maintain enough side distance from the cyclists with oncoming traffic
- I can't cross the guideline

2.1.06-028-M.comment: Because of the curve and the trees, you can't see the further road layout well enough. Outside built-up areas, you must maintain a minimum side distance of 2 meters from cyclists. If oncoming traffic suddenly appears, you might not be able to maintain that distance while overtaking. That's why you can't overtake here.

2.1.06-029-M.question_text: Why are you not allowed to overtake here?

options.text: Because the side distance to the cyclists becomes too small
Because there's a risk to oncoming traffic
Because the guideline can't be crossed

2.1.06-029-M.comment: The road is too narrow to maintain enough side distance to both the cyclists and oncoming traffic.

2.1.06-030.question_text: You're about to overtake on a tree-lined avenue. What special thing should you keep in mind?

options.text: Side distances are often misjudged here
Vehicles with high bodies often avoid branches
The frequency of tree accidents is particularly high here

2.1.06-030.comment: The avenue is lined with trees, which can make it easy to misjudge distances because of the changing light and shadows. There can also be accidents with trees and vehicles with high bodies trying to avoid branches.

2.1.06-103-M.question_text: Why do you need to switch to the right lane now?

options.text: - red cars
- blue cars
- yellow tractor

2.1.06-103-M.comment: The traffic sign shows a narrowing (end of a lane) in 200 meters. The lane will lead into oncoming traffic due to the narrowing, so you need to be especially alert to avoid ending up in the wrong lane.

options.text: I won't overtake the cyclists for now
I will overtake the cyclists
I will honk to get the cyclists to ride single file

2.1.06-104-M.comment: You shouldn't overtake for now because they're riding side by side, and you can't maintain enough distance.

2.1.06-105.question_text: How should you behave correctly now?

options.text: I slow down to walking speed
I drive as far right as possible
I drive past the pedestrians

2.1.06-105.comment: In this situation, you need to slow down to walking speed and keep as far right as possible. You shouldn't drive past the pedestrians because it poses too much danger.

2.1.06-106-M.question_text: How should you behave correctly now?

options.text: I reduce my speed
I keep my speed
I overtake the cyclist

2.1.06-106-M.comment: You need to reduce your speed because you can't maintain enough distance from the cyclist.

2.1.07-006-B.question_text: You're approaching the vehicles shown. How do you behave?

options.text: Watch to see if the tractor stays on the shoulder
Allow the tractor to switch to the road if it signals left
If the tractor signals left, use your high beams and pass quickly

2.1.07-006-B.comment: Outside of built-up areas, slow vehicles like tractors, trucks, and mopeds often drive on the paved shoulder, making it easier to overtake them. If such a vehicle wants to turn left or needs to return to the main road for other reasons, you should allow it to change lanes.

2.1.07-008-M.question_text: The white car wants to turn left. How should you behave if the car doesn't stop?

options.text: I reduce my speed
I give up my right of way
I honk and continue at the same speed

2.1.07-008-M.comment: The white car wants to turn left, and since you don't know if it will stop (you have the right of way), it's better to give up your right of way and slow down just in case.

2.1.07-009-M.question_text: Why do you need to brake now?

options.text: - green vehicle
- motorcycle
- yellow car

2.1.07-009-M.comment: You should brake because the green vehicle seems to be coming onto the road behind the tractor.

2.1.07-010-M.question_text: What should you expect in this parking lot?

options.text: With incorrectly parked trucks
With vehicles pulling out
With people on the road

2.1.07-010-M.comment: Vehicles can leave the parking lot, so watch out for vehicles pulling out. People might walk on the road because they're taking a break. Truck drivers often park in car parking spaces.

2.1.07-014-M.question_text: What should you expect in this situation?

options.text: The driver of the red vehicle might not see me
The green truck is turning around
The tractor is driving on the road

2.1.07-014-M.comment: Because of the turning truck, the delivery van might not see you. Be ready to brake.

2.1.07-015-M.question_text: Why should you reduce your speed here?

options.text: Because the red car might swerve into my lane
Because more people might enter the road
Because the blue car might keep going

2.1.07-015-M.comment: It's unlikely that the car on the left lane will move since it seems to have broken down. Even if it does, it won't affect you. However, since there's a person on the road, you need to be especially careful. It's also possible that more people might get out of the vehicle and run onto the road. The parked car might be hidden by the bushes, or there might not be a warning triangle set up. The car behind you might not realize in time that the vehicle in front has stopped. So, you should drive cautiously and expect that the car behind might swerve into your lane.

options.text: I keep braking
I switch to the left lane
I keep driving steadily

2.1.07-018.comment: Since there's a car behind you on the tram lane and the cyclist seems to be coming onto the road from the right, you should keep braking.

options.text: I drive as far right as possible
I brake
I switch to the left lane

2.1.07-020.comment: The yellow car is coming towards you as a wrong-way driver on the highway. Drive as far right as you can and brake. To warn other road users, turn on your hazard lights.

2.1.07-022-M.question_text: How should you behave in this situation?

options.text: Keep reducing speed
Be ready to brake
Perform an emergency stop

2.1.07-022-M.comment: Animals on the road can be unpredictable. You should keep reducing your speed and pay close attention to the situation. If the animals run onto the road, you should be ready to brake. An emergency stop could lead to a rear-end collision if the vehicle behind you can't react quickly enough.

2.1.07-023-M.question_text: Why should you reduce your speed now?

options.text: Because of the animal
Because of the red car
Because of the speed limit

2.1.07-023-M.comment: Even if you're following the speed limit of 60 km/h, an animal is running onto the road right in front of you. To avoid an accident, you need to slow down. The oncoming car doesn't affect your driving.

2.1.07-101.question_text: When can a fast-moving car skid sideways on a dry, straight road?

options.text: When it's suddenly hit by strong crosswinds
When a tire bursts
When there's suddenly headwind

2.1.07-101.comment: A vehicle on a straight, dry road can skid sideways due to strong crosswinds or a burst tire. In that case, immediately ease off the gas, steer against it, and brake gently.

2.1.07-102.question_text: What makes driving in a convoy easier?

options.text: Watching the convoy through the windows of the vehicles ahead
Slightly offset driving in your own lane
Driving with hazard lights constantly on

2.1.07-102.comment: Slightly offset driving allows you to see the vehicles ahead. This way, you can see past the car in front or through its windows to assess the traffic situation and react more quickly to sudden events. Driving with hazard lights in a convoy is generally prohibited.

2.1.07-106.question_text: If a tire bursts while driving fast on the highway, how should you behave?

options.text: Ease off the gas, steer against it, and brake gently
Pull over to the shoulder, turn on hazard lights, and set up a warning triangle
Immediately perform a full brake and then switch to the shoulder

2.1.07-106.comment: Avoid a full brake on the highway; instead, steer against it and brake gently to stabilize your vehicle. If possible, bring your vehicle to a stop on the shoulder. Turn on your hazard lights and set up your warning triangle to warn following vehicles.

2.1.07-109.question_text: You increase your speed from 50 km/h to 100 km/h. How does the braking distance change according to the rule of thumb?

options.text: It quadruples from 25 m to 100 m
It doubles from 15 m to 30 m
It halves from 50 m to 25 m

2.1.07-109.comment: According to the rule of thumb, the braking distance quadruples when the speed doubles. For example, at 40 km/h, it's 16 meters, and at 80 km/h, it's 64 meters.

2.1.07-111.question_text: Why do you need to be ready to brake in this situation?

options.text: Because the other vehicle might keep going
Because the road layout requires it
Because a speed limit is visible

2.1.07-111.comment: You see a vehicle trying to enter the road from the right. Since it's coming from a field or forest path, you have the right of way. The trees might limit visibility for the driver. It's possible they might continue despite having to wait. That's why you need to be ready to brake until you clearly see that they stop.

2.1.07-112.question_text: Why should you reduce your speed now?

options.text: Because I'm hard to see for other road users
Because the road layout requires it
Because I need to yield the right of way

2.1.07-112.comment: You generally have the right of way since you're on a main road. However, to avoid a dangerous situation, you should still slow down and be ready to brake, as the driver of the car coming from the right might not see you in time or might completely overlook you. The trees at the roadside significantly limit their visibility.

2.1.07-113-M.question_text: How should you behave in this situation?

options.text: I slow down
I speed up
I keep driving at a steady speed

2.1.07-113-M.comment: Since the left lane is narrowing and the vehicle next to you is in that lane and needs to turn right, you should slow down here.

2.1.07-114-M.question_text: What should you expect in this situation?

options.text: - A motorcyclist braking
- A tractor continuing to drive
- A tractor waiting

2.1.07-114-M.comment: Even though you're on a main road, you should always be prepared for dangerous situations. The tractor driver approaching your road at an intersection might not yield and could force the vehicle in front of you to brake. By driving defensively, you can help avoid potentially dangerous situations.

2.1.07-115.question_text: How should you behave in this situation?

options.text: I maintain my speed and keep driving
I speed up to create a safe distance
I brake briefly so the driver behind can reduce speed

2.1.07-115.comment: In this situation, you should maintain your speed and keep driving as you are.

2.1.07-117-M.question_text: What do you need to pay attention to when turning right?

options.text: To the motorcycle
To vehicles coming from the left
To the tractor

2.1.07-117-M.comment: You must yield the right of way to all vehicles on the main road. The motorcycle is in the lane you want to turn into. Before you turn right onto the main road, you need to wait and let the motorcycle pass.

2.1.07-119.question_text: What should you do if a collision with wildlife is unavoidable?

options.text: I brake as hard as I can
I maintain my direction
I always swerve

2.1.07-119.comment: If a collision with an animal can't be avoided, you should maintain your direction. Brake hard and keep a firm grip on the steering wheel. Swerving can put other road users at risk or lead to greater damage than a controlled collision with the animal.

2.1.07-120-M.question_text: Your vehicle's cruise control is set to 130 km/h. How should you behave now?

options.text: - Restore the safe distance by braking
- Overtake the motorcycle
- Switch to the right lane

2.1.07-120-M.comment: You need to deactivate the cruise control by braking. The motorcyclist is entering your safe distance. You can only restore this distance by braking. Switching to the right lane isn't possible because you'd enter the safe distance of the vehicles behind you. Accelerating is not allowed due to the speed limit of 130 km/h.

2.1.07-121-M.question_text: How should you behave in this situation?

options.text: I brake hard immediately
I don't swerve
I swerve to the left

2.1.07-121-M.comment: In this situation, you should brake hard immediately but also avoid swerving.

options.text: Reduce speed, be ready to brake
Switch to the left lane
Keep driving, signal your intention

2.1.07-202.comment: A car in front of you is parking. You need to reduce your speed and can only switch lanes to avoid the parking car after the motorcycle has passed you.

2.1.07-203.question_text: What do you need to know about using the rearview mirrors?

options.text: I can't see vehicles and pedestrians in the blind spot
Mirrors must be adjusted for the driver
The inside mirror has no blind spot to the right

2.1.07-203.comment: Here’s what you need to know about using rearview mirrors: 1. Before starting your drive, mirrors must be adjusted for the driver. 2. All types of mirrors have blind spots. These are areas you can't see where pedestrians, small vehicles, or obstacles can be missed. By properly adjusting the outside mirrors and the inside mirror, you can minimize the blind spot as much as possible.

2.1.07-204.question_text: You're driving into a right curve. A motorcyclist is coming towards you at high speed. What dangers should you expect?

options.text: - might lean into my lane due to a strong tilt
- might cut the curve and enter my lane
- will brake in time and not enter my lane

2.1.07-204.comment: As you enter a right curve, the oncoming motorcyclist is in a left curve. Their upper body is leaning towards you. Keep in mind that the motorcyclist is almost as wide as a car. If they ride too close to the center line to widen the curve and reduce centrifugal forces, their upper body could be hit by your vehicle.

2.1.07-206.question_text: You're on a country road. In front of you, there's a slow-moving line of about 15 vehicles. What should you do?

options.text: I'll stay behind the line of vehicles for now
I'll use my horn and blink to encourage those ahead to overtake
I'll overtake the line of vehicles as quickly as possible
